summary: Prepared a separate fixed Admin recovery for sale 16954 after a preserved pre-sale backup proved product 5370 cost USD 170/KHR 0. The v2 no-store preview is digest-bound and requires backup_restore; apply requires a same-origin exact body, rate/body gates and a fresh backup, then adds one USD 185/KHR 752,025 line and one fully released allocation in one D1 batch with an append-only v2 receipt, non-reversible history and provenance audit. Because the sale remains awaiting payment, v2 does not change product, branch or lot stock and creates no movement. Receipt-backed replay remains valid after later legitimate sale or product changes, and ambiguous post-commit reads use the same verification_pending and HTTP 202 uncertain contracts as v1.
changes: Added a dedicated saleIncidentRecoveryV2 helper with fixed sale 16954, product 5370, pre-sale cost evidence, current product revision, unique-positive-lot, header and zero-effect fingerprints.

Added separate v2 preview/apply routes with backup_restore permission, no-store, same-origin, 4KB body, rate, backup-first, exact digest-bound request, receipt reconciliation and post-commit cache/broadcast handling.

Added one atomic D1 batch that inserts the v2 receipt, one explicit-null/zero-discount line, one fully released allocation, one non-reversible history/member and one redacted audit; it does not update header money or stock and does not insert a movement.

Added focused real-Hono migrated-SQLite coverage for permission, frozen preview, exact apply, v1 receipt coexistence, later-activity replay, lot race rollback, lost response, uncertainty, verification pending, audit rollback, backup failure, origin, body and rate gates.

risks: V2 intentionally fails closed if sale 16954, product 5370, its stock revision or unique positive lot changes before apply; a new reviewed fingerprint would then be required.
Lot 56737 is recorded as recovery-time unique-positive-lot attribution, not as historical proof of the originally selected lot.
Migration 0145 and the reviewed v1 runtime must already be live before these routes can work; a missing migration returns 409 before backup or mutation.
Independent exact-head review and release gates remain required before the v2 Worker/UI can be deployed or applied.
